title: Alira: a huge facilities deck beside Metropark's lakeside park.
excerpt: An 832-unit block in Metropark Subang with one of the biggest facility decks Sean has seen and a back door to the township's lakeside park. He likes the township and the compact layout, but finds the doors awkward.
takeaways: A 695 sq ft one-plus-one corner unit resells for about RM450,000 and asks about RM3,000 a month in rent.
A new retail strip with a Mercato grocer means residents can spend a weekend without driving.
The facility deck is vast and varied, but empty land nearby means more construction to come.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Alira's two towers hold 832 units, with 16 units and four lifts per floor, around a facilities deck so large it takes a while to walk: a lap pool with a blue safety line, a jacuzzi reached from the pool, a covered spa pavilion with saunas, a glass-walled gym, separate playgrounds for toddlers and older children, a wing chun corner, a futsal cage, a garden kitchen, a function hall, a library and a karaoke room. The management office and a lounge sit in the wide entrance lobby.

Sean viewed a 695 sq ft corner unit with one bedroom, a study and one bathroom, and a ceiling of nearly 3 m. The yard is folded into the kitchen, which comes with a Teka hob and hood. The single bathroom opens to both the hallway and the bedroom, which lets the bedroom run about 6 m long, and windows fill almost the whole facade.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Alira is part of the Metropark township in Subang, after the earlier Pandora, Paloma and Paisley blocks, with wide roads and pavements, direct access from the Federal Highway and USJ Heights nearby. A back gate opens onto the township's mature lakeside park and cycle path, which leads to an international school, and the newly opened South Place retail has a Mercato grocer, clinics and eateries. The Hi-Tech Industrial Park and a line of pylons are in view.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Property listings show subsale prices of about RM450,000 for this unit size, about RM700 psf, with asking rents of about RM3,000 a month.

standout.title: Rooms within the deck
standout.body: The deck mixes sunken and raised areas, a jacuzzi you step into from the pool, and glass boxes for the library, karaoke and gym. Each family gathering can have its own space and privacy even when many residents come down at once, and no corner is wasted.

pros: The township concept: the park was ready from the first phase, its trees are now mature, and with the retail open you can live a whole weekend here without a car, a lifestyle he says only this part of Subang offers.
The architecture: a wide entrance lobby with the management office and lounge built in, and a huge, varied facilities deck between the towers that gives both blocks breathing space.
The layout: in a corner unit, the yard merges into the kitchen and the single bathroom frees a 6 m-long bedroom, with full-width windows and a flexible study, suiting a couple who work from home.
cons: The concept took about seven years to come together, so early buyers waited a long time for the commercial area that makes it work.

Design quirks: a plain exterior, a big drop between the garden units and the deck that needs many ramps and steps, and a glass door plus an outward-opening fire door at the lift lobby that can swing into people. Intermediate units may face overlooking from neighbouring blocks.
The township is still growing: empty land in front means more construction noise and either more competition or a new catalyst, and he doesn't know who owns it.

closing: Park-side living with convenience on the doorstep, finally complete after years of waiting, for couples and families who value the lifestyle over a short-term gain.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this December 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit after completion; prices and rents are from listings as he quoted them.
